S&P 500 Equity Health Screener

Financial health, forensic accounting checks and peer-relative ranking, computed from SEC filings. No estimates, no price targets, no buy or sell verdicts.

Methodology and limitations

Sector rank is peer-relative, computed in two steps: percentile rank within sector on six metrics, then a rank of that composite. A mean of percentiles is not itself a percentile — it compresses toward 0.5 and never reaches 1 — so the second step is what makes the number mean what the label says.

Sector benchmarks use the median, never the mean. Valuation multiples are right-skewed; one company at 400x drags a mean far above anything a typical constituent trades at.

Not every metric applies to every sector. Banks, insurers and property trusts report no cost of revenue, so they have no gross margin. Altman Z was estimated on manufacturers. A missing value is excluded from the health score rather than counted as a failure — a company is never marked down for not reporting something its accounting framework does not contain.

Annual data only. Every figure is as of the last filed 10-K and can be up to twelve months old. For a company mid-cycle the gap to current trading can be large.

There are no recommendations, by design. A public site telling people whether to invest is giving investment advice, a regulated activity in most jurisdictions, and a verdict built on data this stale would be confidently wrong often enough to cause real losses.
